title: CCST Networking (100-150) practice exam
note: Original questions written for MyNextCert from Cisco's public 100-150 CCST Networking exam objectives (checked 2026-11-26). Not real exam questions. Cisco doesn't publish the number of items or the topic weights, so this is a 45-item stand-in that fits the real 50 minutes, with an even split across the six domains and 4 hands-on items.

q.q: A switch receives an Ethernet frame on one port and must decide where to send it. Which address does it read, and at which OSI layer?
o: The destination IP address, at Layer 3
A router reads the IP address to route packets. A basic switch does not look at it to forward a frame.
The destination port number, at Layer 4
Port numbers belong to TCP and UDP. A plain switch ignores them.
The destination MAC address, at Layer 2 of the OSI model
Right. Switches forward frames using the MAC address in the frame header, and the frame is the Layer 2 data unit.
The source MAC address only, at Layer 1
Layer 1 carries bits, not addresses. The switch learns the source MAC but forwards by the destination.

q.q: A PC sends a web request. Which list shows the data units from the one built first to the one sent on the wire?
o: Data, then segment, then packet, then frame
Right. Each layer wraps the one above: TCP adds a header to make a segment, IP makes a packet, and Ethernet makes a frame.
Frame, then packet, then segment, then data
This is the order the receiver unwraps the data, not the order the sender builds it.
Packet, then segment, then frame, then data
The segment is made by TCP before IP wraps it into a packet.
Data, then frame, then segment, then packet
The frame is the last wrapper added, because it needs the next-hop MAC address.

q.q: A link is rated at 1 Gbps. A file copy over it runs at about 300 Mbps. What does the 300 Mbps figure describe?
o: Bandwidth, the highest rate the link can carry
Bandwidth is the 1 Gbps rating, the ceiling. The copy rate is what actually happened.
Latency, the time one packet takes to arrive
Latency is measured in milliseconds, not Mbps.
Jitter, the change in delay between packets
Jitter is also a time measure, so it is not a data rate.
Throughput, the real rate you get in practice
Right. Throughput is the real rate you get. Overhead, errors, congestion and slow devices keep it below the rated bandwidth.

q.q: You want the real speed between a PC and a server in the same building, without involving the internet. Which method fits best?
o: Open an internet speed-test website on the PC
That test measures your path to an outside test server, not the path to your own server.
Run iperf with the PC and server as its two ends
Right. iperf makes traffic between two hosts you choose and reports the throughput between them.
Ping the server and read the reply time
Ping reports delay in milliseconds. It does not measure how much data per second can flow.
Run tracert to the server and count the hops
Tracert lists the routers on the path. It says nothing about speed.

q.q: One organization owns the cabling that joins six buildings on a single campus. What type of network is this?
o: A personal area network (PAN)
A PAN is a few devices around one person, like a phone and a headset.
A campus area network (CAN)
Right. A CAN links several buildings of one organization in a small area such as a base or a college.
A wide area network (WAN)
A WAN spans long distances, usually over a provider's links, such as city to city.
A wireless LAN (WLAN)
A WLAN is a LAN that uses Wi-Fi. The question says the buildings are joined by owned cabling.

q.q: In a star topology, every device connects to one central switch. What happens if that switch loses power?
o: Only the device nearest the switch is affected
Distance does not matter. Each cable ends at the same switch.
The devices form a ring and keep talking
A star has no ring path. Devices do not link to each other directly.
Traffic reroutes through the closest neighbor PC
End devices do not forward traffic for others in a star.
Every device loses its path to the others
Right. The switch is the single center, so with it down no one can talk through it.

q.q: A unit stops running its own mail servers. A vendor hosts, patches and runs the email, and users sign in with a browser. Which service model is this?
o: Software as a Service, or SaaS, model
Right. In SaaS the vendor runs everything and you only use the finished application.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
In IaaS you rent servers and storage but install and patch the software yourself.
Platform as a Service (PaaS)
PaaS gives developers a place to run their own code. Here the customer only uses the app.
A private cloud on the unit's own hardware
The vendor, not the unit, runs the service, so this is not a private cloud.

q.q: A unit keeps its records on its own servers and rents a public cloud to host its public website for busy periods. What is this mix called?
o: A community cloud
A community cloud is shared by several groups with the same needs. It is not a mix of private and public.
Only a public cloud
The records stay on the unit's own servers, so some of the setup is not public.
A hybrid cloud of both kinds
Right. A hybrid cloud combines private or on-premises resources with a public cloud.
Only a private cloud
Part of the load runs on a rented public cloud, so it is not purely private.

q.q: Which application would most likely choose UDP over TCP?
o: A file transfer needing every byte in order
This needs TCP, which resends lost data and keeps the order.
A secure web login, where errors must be corrected
HTTPS runs over TCP so that nothing is lost or reordered.
An email attachment, where nothing may be missing
Mail protocols use TCP for reliable delivery.
A live voice call, where late data is useless
Right. UDP is connectionless and has low delay. A late voice packet is useless, so resending it would not help.

q.q: Logs from a switch and a server disagree by several minutes, which makes an incident timeline hard to build. Which protocol keeps device clocks in step to prevent this?
o: DNS
DNS turns names into IP addresses. It does not set clocks.
NTP
Right. The Network Time Protocol syncs clocks to a time source. Matching times make logs far easier to read.
DHCP
DHCP hands out IP settings. Clock sync is not its job.
ICMP
ICMP carries error and test messages such as ping. It does not sync time.

q.q: Which TWO protocols encrypt the data they carry? (Choose two.)
o: HTTPS
Right. HTTPS wraps web traffic in TLS encryption.
FTP
FTP sends data and passwords in clear text.
SFTP
Right. SFTP carries file transfers inside an encrypted SSH session.
TFTP
TFTP has no login or encryption.
HTTP
HTTP sends web data in clear text.

q.q: Which of these addresses can NOT be routed on the public internet because it is private?
o: This is just outside the 172.16 to 172.31 private range, so it is a public address.
The private block is 192.168.0.0/16. 192.169 is a public address.
Right. The private range 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255 includes 172.20.4.9. Internet routers drop private addresses.
Only 10.0.0.0/8 is private in the 10 range. 11.0.0.1 is public.

q.q: A home router lets six devices with private addresses share one public address, telling them apart by port number. What is this called?
o: NAT overload, also called PAT
Right. Many inside addresses share one outside address, and the router tracks each flow by its port number.
Static NAT with one fixed address
Static NAT maps one inside address to one fixed outside address, with no sharing.
DHCP relay for address requests
A relay passes DHCP requests to a server. It does not change addresses.
Reverse DNS lookups
Reverse DNS finds a name for an address. It does not translate packets.

q.q: An address of 150.20.3.4 falls in which default classful range?
o: Class B, first octet 128 to 191
Right. The first octet 150 sits in the Class B range of 128 to 191.
Class A, first octet 1 to 126
Class A ends at 126, so 150 is out of it.
Class C, first octet 192 to 223
192 to 223 begins above 150.
Class D, 224 to 239
Class D is multicast and starts at 224.

q.q: How many usable host addresses does the 192.168.10.0/26 subnet have?
o: 64 is the total, but two of them are reserved, so only 62 can be given to hosts.
30 hosts is the answer for a /27, which has 5 host bits.
Right. A /26 leaves 6 host bits, so 2 to the 6th is 64 addresses. Take away the network and broadcast addresses to get 62.
126 hosts is the answer for a /25, which has 7 host bits.

q.q: Which slash notation matches the subnet mask 255.255.255.240?
o: /27, leaving 5 host bits
/28, leaving 4 host bits
Right. The last octet 240 is 11110000, so 4 extra bits are added to 24, giving 28.
/29, leaving 3 host bits
/26, leaving 6 host bits

q.q: A host has the address 10.1.1.200/25. What is the broadcast address of its subnet?
o: 10.1.1.127, end of the lower block
This is the broadcast of the lower block, 10.1.1.0 to 10.1.1.127.
10.1.1.191, end of a /26 block
This would be the end of a /26 block, not a /25.
10.1.1.200, the host itself
This is the host's own address, not the last address of the subnet.
10.1.1.255, the last address
Right. With /25 the blocks are 128 big. 200 falls in the block 10.1.1.128 to 10.1.1.255, and the last address is the broadcast.

q.q: Two PCs use a /26 mask. PC1 is 192.168.5.70 and PC2 is 192.168.5.130. Which statement is true?
o: They share one subnet and talk directly through a switch
They would share a subnet only if both fell in the same 64-address block.
They share one broadcast domain because the first three octets match
Matching octets are not enough. The mask decides where the network ends.
They are in different subnets and need a router to talk
Right. A /26 splits the last octet into blocks of 64. .70 is in 64 to 127 and .130 is in 128 to 191.
They cannot talk at all, even through a router
A router can pass traffic between two different subnets.

q.q: Which is a correct short form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?
o: Right. Drop leading zeros in each group and replace one run of all-zero groups with a double colon.
A double colon may appear only once, and it is not used at the end here.
Two double colons would make the address ambiguous, so this is not allowed.
This has only four groups, so it is not a full 128-bit address.

q.q: An interface shows an IPv6 address that starts with fe80. What kind of address is this?
o: Global unicast, routed on the internet
Global addresses start with 2 or 3 today, not fe80.
Multicast, sent to a group of hosts
Multicast addresses start with ff.
Loopback, used to test the host itself
The IPv6 loopback address is ::1.
Link-local, for the local link only
Right. Addresses in fe80::/10 are for the local link and are not routed beyond it. Devices create one on every IPv6 interface.

q.q: In the address 2001:db8:acad:1::5/64, what does the 64 mean?
o: The subnet holds only 64 hosts in total
A /64 holds a huge number of hosts, since 64 host bits remain.
The leading 64 bits name the network
Right. The prefix length counts the leading bits that identify the network. The remaining 64 bits identify the host.
The address may cross at most 64 routers
That would be a hop limit, not a prefix length.
The router has 64 subnets
The prefix length says nothing about how many subnets there are.

q.q: IPv6 has no broadcast. How does a host reach all other nodes on the local link?
o: It sends to ::1
::1 is the loopback address, which only reaches the host itself.
It sends to ff02::1
Right. ff02::1 is the all-nodes link-local multicast group, which does the job broadcast did in IPv4.
This is an IPv4 broadcast address, not an IPv6 one.
It sends to fe80::/10
This is a prefix for link-local unicast addresses, not a group address.

q.q: Which cable is not affected by electrical interference and suits long runs between buildings?
o: Unshielded twisted pair, Cat 6
UTP can pick up noise and is limited to about 100 meters.
Coaxial cable
Coax is shielded, but it is copper and still carries electrical signals.
RJ-11 telephone cable
RJ-11 is a connector used for phone lines, not a long-distance data cable.
Fiber-optic cable
Right. Fiber carries light, so electrical noise cannot reach it, and it travels far.

q.q: Which connector is on the end of a standard Ethernet twisted-pair patch cable?
o: RJ-45
Right. RJ-45 has 8 pins and fits Ethernet ports on PCs, switches and routers.
RJ-11
RJ-11 is smaller, with 4 or 6 pins, and is used for telephone lines.
F-type
F-type is the threaded connector on cable-TV coax.
LC
LC is a small fiber connector, not used on copper cable.

q.q: Which wireless band is the most crowded and is hurt by microwave ovens and Bluetooth devices?
o: 5 GHz
5 GHz has more channels and fewer competing devices.
6 GHz
6 GHz is newer and has the most room, so it is quiet.
2.4 GHz
Right. This band has few channels and is shared by many unlicensed devices, so interference is common.
Cellular licensed spectrum
Cellular carriers own their frequencies, so ovens and Bluetooth do not share them.

q.q: A Cat 6 run keeps showing errors. It was laid right beside a bundle of power cables and a fluorescent light ballast. What is the most likely cause?
o: A fiber connector that is dirty
This is a copper cable, so fiber connectors are not involved.
Too many devices on the 2.4 GHz band
The problem is on a wired cable, so Wi-Fi bands do not matter.
A cellular tower that is too far away
Cellular signals are not carried on this cable.
Electrical noise on the copper cable
Right. Power cables and ballasts give off electrical noise that copper twisted pair can pick up.

q.q: What is one advantage of cellular networks over home Wi-Fi?
o: It runs on unlicensed bands any device may share
Unlicensed bands are what Wi-Fi uses, and many devices share them.
The carrier controls the licensed spectrum it uses
Right. Licensed spectrum is controlled by the carrier, so other users cannot use it at will.
It needs no carrier, plan or subscription of any kind
Cellular service runs through a carrier and normally needs a plan.
Its signal never weakens with distance or walls
Signal strength still falls with distance and some walls.

q.q: A badge reader, a smart thermostat and an IP camera all join the network. What group of endpoints do they belong to?
o: Servers
Servers share resources with many clients. These are small single-purpose devices.
Network infrastructure devices
Infrastructure means switches, routers and similar gear that moves traffic.
Internet of Things devices
Right. IoT devices are everyday objects with a network connection and little computing power.
Mobile computing devices
Mobile devices are phones and tablets. These devices are fixed in place.

q.q: Which endpoint is normally powered through a PoE switch port and carries voice calls?
o: An IP phone on the desk
Right. IP phones usually draw power from the Ethernet cable and send voice as network traffic.
A rack server
Servers use their own power supplies and need far more power than PoE gives.
A desktop computer
Desktops plug into a wall outlet.
A laser printer
Printers also use wall power and are not voice devices.

q.q: On a Windows PC, which command shows the IP address, mask, default gateway and DNS servers together?
o: ipconfig /all
Right. The /all switch gives the full detail for each adapter, including DNS and DHCP details.
ping -t
Ping tests reachability over and over. It does not list adapter settings.
tracert
Tracert lists the routers on a path to a destination.
ipconfig /flushdns
This clears the cache of stored DNS answers and shows no settings.

q.q: Which command shows the IP addresses on the interfaces of a modern Linux computer?
o: ipconfig
This is the Windows command, so it does not exist on most Linux systems.
nslookup
Nslookup asks a DNS server for the address of a name.
ip addr
Right. The ip command is the current tool and ip addr lists addresses on every interface.
traceroute
Traceroute shows the path to a destination, not the local addresses.

q.q: A phone sees the network named CG-Guest but will not join. Which settings must match the router's setup?
o: The DNS server and the subnet mask
These are IP settings handed out after the phone has joined.
The security type and the passphrase
Right. The client must offer the same authentication method and the correct key as the access point.
The router's serial number and brand
The phone never uses these to join the network.
The default gateway and the NTP server
These matter after connecting. They do not decide whether the phone can join.

q.q: On a Cisco Catalyst access port, a solid amber LED usually means:
o: The port is forwarding traffic normally
Normal operation is solid or blinking green.
No cable is plugged in at all
An unused port is usually dark with no light.
The port is carrying heavy traffic
Heavy traffic makes a green light blink faster, not turn amber.
Up but not forwarding, often blocked by spanning tree
Right. Solid amber usually means the port is up but not forwarding, often because spanning tree has blocked it.

q.q: A technician sees the link light of a switch port is solid green. What does this tell them?
o: The link has failed
A failed link shows no light or an amber one.
The port is transferring data heavily
Activity shows as blinking, not as a steady light.
A link is up, but nothing is moving now
Right. Green means the device on the other end is connected. Blinking green would show activity.
The port has been turned off by the administrator
A shut-down port stays dark.

q.q: A diagram tells you to prepare a new router for first-time setup from a laptop with no network yet. Which cable do you attach?
o: A console cable to the router's console port
Right. The console port gives local command-line access without any IP network.
An Ethernet cable from the laptop to a WAN port
The router has no address configured yet, so you cannot reach it over the network.
A fiber patch cable to an SFP slot
The laptop has no fiber port, and fiber is not used for first setup.
A power cable to the laptop's USB port
Power cables feed the router. They do not give a setup connection.

q.q: A rack diagram shows two core switches, each plugged into a different power feed. Why?
o: To double the speed of both switches
Two power feeds do not change the speed of the switches.
To let the switches share one IP address
Power has nothing to do with IP addressing.
To save cable by using shorter patch cords
Two feeds usually need more cable, not less, and cable length is a separate topic.
One failure still leaves one switch running
Right. Separate feeds give redundancy, so the other switch stays on if one circuit trips.

q.q: An engineer needs command-line access to a switch even though the network is down. Which port is for this?
o: A GigabitEthernet port
Ethernet ports need a working network and an IP address to manage the switch.
The console port
Right. The console port is a direct local management connection and needs no IP network.
An SFP slot
An SFP slot holds a transceiver for network links, not for management.
A PoE port
PoE ports power devices such as phones and access points.

q.q: Which port type holds a small removable module so the same switch can use fiber or copper links?
o: A fixed RJ-45 port
A fixed RJ-45 port is copper only.
An SFP port
Right. SFP is a hot-swappable transceiver slot, and the module decides the cable type.
A console port
The console port is used for management, not for module swapping.
A USB port
A USB port is used for storage or console access, not for fiber modules.

q.q: A ceiling access point has no power outlet nearby. Which switch feature lets it get power over the same Ethernet cable?
o: Spanning tree protocol (STP)
Spanning tree prevents loops. It does not supply power.
VLAN trunking (802.1Q tags)
Trunking carries many VLANs on one link and has nothing to do with power.
Port mirroring to a sensor
Mirroring copies traffic to another port for analysis.
Power over Ethernet (PoE) on the port
Right. PoE sends power and data together over twisted pair, so no outlet is needed at the device.

q.q: A PC at 192.168.1.20/24 sends a packet to 10.5.5.5. Where does the PC send it first?
o: To its default gateway
Right. 10.5.5.5 is outside the local subnet, so the PC hands the packet to the router that is its gateway.
Straight to 10.5.5.5
A host only sends directly to addresses in its own subnet.
To its DNS server
DNS turns names into addresses. It does not forward packets.
To every device by broadcast
Broadcasts stay in the local network and are not used to reach a remote one.

q.q: What does a Layer 3 switch do that a Layer 2 switch cannot?
o: Forward frames by MAC address
Both switch types do this.
Provide power over Ethernet
PoE is a separate feature found on either kind.
Route between IP subnets
Right. A Layer 3 switch can read IP addresses and route between VLANs. A Layer 2 switch only forwards by MAC address.
Learn MAC addresses
Both switch types build a MAC address table.

q.q: A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table. What does it do?
o: Drops the frame
A switch does not drop unknown unicast frames. It floods them.
Sends it back out the port it came in on
A switch never forwards a frame back to its source port.
Sends it to the default gateway only
Switches do not use gateways to forward frames.
Floods it out of all other ports
Right. With an unknown destination the switch sends the frame everywhere else until the right device answers.

q.q: What does creating separate VLANs on one switch do?
o: It joins all ports into one larger broadcast domain
This is the reverse of what VLANs do.
It makes separate broadcast domains
Right. Devices in different VLANs cannot reach each other at Layer 2 and need a router to talk.
It raises the speed of every port
VLANs do not change port speed.
It encrypts all traffic between ports
VLANs separate traffic. They do not encrypt it.

q.q: A switch port allows only devices whose MAC addresses are on an approved list. What is a weakness of this MAC filtering?
o: It blocks every approved device as well
Approved devices are the ones it allows.
It only works with fiber-optic cabling
MAC filtering works on any port type.
An attacker can spoof an approved MAC
Right. An attacker who sees an approved address on the network can set their own device to the same one.
Switches do not support MAC filtering
Many switches and access points support it.

q.q: You think a bad patch cable is why a user has no link. What is the next best troubleshooting step?
o: Test it by swapping in a known good patch cable
Right. A theory is only a guess until it is tested. A quick swap proves or rules out the cable.
Close the ticket and note the cable as the cause
Closing before testing records a guess as a fact.
Escalate to the network engineer straight away
Escalate if the tests fail. A simple swap comes first.
Replace the user's switch for a fresh start
This is costly and needless before the simple test is done.

q.q: Three tickets arrive. A user's mouse is sticky, 80 people on one floor have no network, and a printer is low on toner. Which is first?
o: The outage that blocks the whole floor
Right. Prioritize by how many people are hit and how badly work is blocked. The outage stops 80 people.
The sticky mouse, because it is quickest
A fast fix does not outrank an outage that stops many people.
The printer, because it arrived first
Arrival order matters less than impact.
Whichever the loudest caller reports
Volume of complaint is not the same as impact.

q.q: What is the main purpose of a packet analyzer such as Wireshark?
o: To block malicious traffic at the network edge
That is a firewall's job, and Wireshark only observes.
To hand out IP addresses to new devices
That is done by a DHCP server.
To capture traffic and inspect each packet
Right. It records packets crossing an interface so you can see addresses, protocols and errors.
To store passwords for network devices
That is a password manager's job, not an analyzer's.

q.q: You captured traffic in Wireshark and a colleague wants to open it later on another PC. What should you do?
o: Take a screenshot of the packet list
A screenshot loses the packet data and cannot be re-filtered.
Save it as a .pcap or .pcapng file
Right. These formats keep every packet, so any copy of Wireshark can reopen them.
Print the capture to a text note
A printout cannot be reloaded or searched in Wireshark.
Leave Wireshark open and share the screen
The capture is lost when the program closes unless it is saved.

q.q: A ping to a server times out, yet users load its web page without trouble. What is the most likely reason?
o: The server has no IP address
If it had no address, the web page could not load either.
The web page is cached on the user's PC
A cached copy would not explain a live page loading from the server.
DNS is returning the wrong address
A wrong address would stop the web page loading as well.
A firewall is blocking ICMP echo
Right. Firewalls often drop ping while still allowing web ports, so a timeout does not prove the host is down.

q.q: In a traceroute, hop 4 shows * * * but hops 5 to 8 answer normally and the destination is reached. What does this suggest?
o: The destination host is switched off
The destination answered, so it is up.
The link is broken at hop 4 so nothing passes
If the path were broken, no later hop could answer.
Hop 4 ignores probes but passes traffic
Right. The path works because later hops respond. Many devices are set to ignore these probes.
The local PC has lost its default gateway
The first hops answered, so the PC reaches its gateway.

q.q: ping 8.8.8.8 works, but ping www.example.com says it could not find the host. What is the most likely problem?
o: DNS name resolution is failing
Right. Reaching an address by number proves the network works, so only the step that turns names into addresses is failing.
The default gateway address is wrong
A wrong gateway would also stop the ping by number.
The network cable is unplugged
With the cable out, the ping by number would fail too.
The subnet mask is too short
A wrong mask could break remote access to the address, so ping by number would likely fail.

q.q: An engineer must log in to a branch switch over a remote link, and policy says passwords may not cross the network in clear text. Which access method should the engineer use?
o: Telnet
Telnet sends everything, including passwords, as clear text.
TFTP
TFTP is for file transfers and has no login or encryption.
HTTP
HTTP is for unencrypted web pages, not a device command line.
SSH
Right. Secure Shell encrypts the whole session, including the password.

q.q: A branch uses Cisco Meraki access points and switches. How do administrators normally manage them?
o: By plugging a console cable into every device
A console cable is not needed for normal management.
Through the cloud dashboard in a web browser
Right. Meraki devices call home to the cloud, so one dashboard configures and monitors them.
By sending files with TFTP to each device
Meraki settings are not pushed by hand-copied files.
By telnetting to each one from the data center
Telnet is not the normal way, and it is not secure.

q.q: Which Cisco command shows a short table of each interface's IP address and its up or down status?
o: show version
This shows the software version, uptime and hardware, not interface status.
show ip interface brief
Right. This command lists every interface with its address, status and protocol on one screen.
show cdp neighbors detail
This lists detail about directly connected Cisco devices.
show mac address-table
This lists learned MAC addresses and the ports they were seen on.

q.q: A Cisco prompt reads Router#. Which mode is that?
o: User EXEC mode
User EXEC mode shows the > prompt and only allows limited commands.
Global configuration mode
Global configuration shows (config)# after the name.
Interface configuration mode
Interface mode shows (config-if)# after the name.
Privileged EXEC mode
Right. The # sign marks privileged EXEC mode, where you can run all show commands and enter configuration mode.

q.q: Which command lists directly connected Cisco devices, with their model and the ports that link to them?
o: show cdp neighbors
Right. Cisco Discovery Protocol lets neighbors announce themselves, and this command lists what was heard.
show ip route
This shows the routing table.
show inventory
This lists the parts of the device itself, such as its modules and serial numbers.
show interface status
This lists the status of local ports, not the devices connected to them.

q.q: In show ip route, a line starts with S* and reads 0.0.0.0/0 via 192.168.1.1. What is it?
o: A route learned through OSPF from a neighbor
OSPF routes begin with O.
A network directly connected to the router
Connected networks begin with C.
A static default route via 192.168.1.1
Right. S means static and * marks the candidate default. 0.0.0.0/0 matches every address not matched by a more specific route.
A route to one host at 192.168.1.1
A single host would use a /32 mask, not 0.0.0.0/0.

q.q: A firewall list is read top to bottom. Rule 1 permits TCP 443 to host 10.1.1.5. Rule 2 denies all IP traffic. Which traffic to 10.1.1.5 gets through?
o: All traffic, because the permit is first
The permit matches only TCP 443, so other traffic reaches rule 2.
Only ping, because ICMP is the default
The list has no ICMP permit, so ping is denied.
Nothing, because the deny overrides rule 1
Rules are read in order, and a deny that comes later cannot cancel a match above it.
Only HTTPS traffic, on TCP port 443
Right. The first matching rule wins. Port 443 matches rule 1. Everything else falls to the deny.

q.q: Which approach makes the safest default for a firewall rule set?
o: Permit everything, then deny known bad traffic
You can only block the threats you know about, so new ones get in.
Deny everything, then permit only what is needed
Right. A default deny means anything not listed is blocked, so mistakes fail safe.
Permit all outbound and inbound traffic from trusted users
A user is not a firewall setting, and broad permits hide risks.
Turn the firewall off during testing
A firewall that is off protects nothing.

q.q: A user on the inside starts a web session. The firewall lets the return traffic back in without a separate rule. What feature does this?
o: Static NAT, which maps one fixed address
NAT changes addresses, but it is not what permits return traffic.
MAC filtering on the switch port
MAC filtering allows devices, not connection replies.
Stateful inspection of open connections
Right. A stateful firewall keeps a table of connections started from inside and allows the matching replies.
Port mirroring to a sensor
Mirroring copies traffic for analysis and does not allow or block it.

q.q: An administrator wants to stop plain, unencrypted web browsing yet keep secure browsing. Which TCP port should the firewall block?
o: Port 80
Right. HTTP uses TCP 80 and sends data in clear text. HTTPS uses 443.
Port 443
This is HTTPS, the secure web traffic to be kept.
Port 22
This is SSH for remote command lines.
Port 53
This is DNS, which most browsing needs to look up names.

q.q: An attacker changes payroll amounts while a file is on its way to the finance system. Which part of the CIA triad is broken?
o: Integrity of the data
Right. Integrity means data stays correct and unaltered. Changing the amounts breaks it.
Confidentiality
Confidentiality is about keeping data from being read by the wrong people.
Availability
Availability is about the data and systems being there when needed.
Accountability
This is a related idea about tracing actions, but it is not one of the three CIA parts.

q.q: A user signs in with a password and then types a code from an authenticator app. Why is this stronger than a password alone?
o: It uses two passwords, so guessing is slower
Two passwords are still the same factor, and both can be stolen together.
It encrypts the password on the keyboard
MFA adds another proof. It does not encrypt typing.
Two different kinds of proof, not just a password
Right. Multifactor authentication combines something you know with something you have.
It removes the need for the account to be authorized
Authorization still decides what the user may do once signed in.

q.q: After a bad change broke a router, an auditor wants to see which admin ran which commands, and when. Which AAA function supplies this record?
o: Authentication
Authentication proves who the user is.
Accounting
Right. Accounting keeps a record of actions and usage for auditing and billing.
Authorization
Authorization decides what the user is allowed to do.
Availability
Availability belongs to the CIA triad, not to AAA.

q.q: An email claims your mailbox is full and asks you to sign in through a link. The link's domain is misspelled. What should you do?
o: Click the link, but do not type a password
Just opening a bad link can still load malware or leak details.
Reply and ask the sender to confirm
Replying tells the attacker the address is live and may lead to more attacks.
Forward it to coworkers as a warning
Forwarding spreads the risk. Report it to security instead.
Do not click it, report it as phishing
Right. A fake sign-in page steals passwords. Reporting helps the security team warn others.

q.q: What role does Active Directory commonly play on a network?
o: It assigns IP addresses to devices
That is the job of a DHCP server.
It filters traffic between networks
That is the job of a firewall.
An identity store of user accounts and groups
Right. Computers ask the directory to check who a user is and which groups they belong to.
It translates private addresses to public ones
That is the job of NAT on a router.

q.q: Which TWO of these are types of malware? (Choose two.)
o: Ransomware
Right. Ransomware locks files and demands payment.
Phishing
Phishing is a trick to steal information, usually by message, not a program.
Spyware
Right. Spyware is software that secretly watches what a user does.
Spam
Spam is unwanted bulk mail, which may carry malware but is not a program itself.
A denial-of-service attack
DoS is an attack that overwhelms a service. It is not a type of software.

q.q: Which wireless security setting is the strongest choice for a new home router, if all devices support it?
o: WPA3
Right. WPA3 is the newest standard and resists password-guessing attacks better than the older ones.
WPA2
WPA2 is still acceptable, but WPA3 is stronger.
WEP
WEP is broken and can be cracked in minutes.
Open, with no password
An open network offers no protection.

q.q: A small office has twenty employees and no authentication server. Which wireless security setup fits best?
o: WPA2 Enterprise, so each person signs in
Enterprise gives each person a sign-in, but it needs a RADIUS or similar authentication server, which this office does not have.
Neither, because small offices need no security
Any network that carries business data needs protection.
Open mode with MAC filtering only
Open mode sends data unencrypted, and MAC addresses can be spoofed.
WPA2 Personal, which uses one shared passphrase
Right. Personal mode needs only a pre-shared key. Enterprise needs a RADIUS server for individual sign-ins.

q.q: When setting up a new home router, which step should come first, apart from choosing WPA3 or WPA2?
o: Turn on remote administration from the internet
This opens the router's admin page to the world and adds risk.
Change the default administrator password
Right. Default logins are public, so anyone on the network could take over the router.
Leave the default network name and password
Default settings are well known and easy to guess.
Disable the router's firewall for speed
The firewall protects the home network, so keep it on.

q.title: Cable up the new office closet
q.scenario: You are setting up a small office from an engineer's diagram. The internet hand-off box is already on the wall and has an Ethernet copper (RJ-45) port. The diagram needs a path from that box to the router, then a switch, then the devices the office uses. Place each device in its spot. Three devices in the tray do not belong in this design.
q.ticket: Work order WO-212: new closet. Ceiling access point has no power outlet. The file server needs a wired gigabit link.

slots.label: Spot A
slots.hint: the hand-off box cable plugs into its WAN port; it is the LAN's default gateway

slots.label: Spot B
slots.hint: the router's LAN port plugs in here; it has PoE ports

slots.label: Spot C
slots.hint: gets data and power on one cable from the switch

slots.label: Spot D
slots.hint: wired to a gigabit switch port with a patch cable

devs.name: Router
devs.why: The hand-off box connects to the router's WAN port, and the router sends traffic between the office LAN and the internet. Its address is what the PCs use as their default gateway.

devs.name: PoE switch
devs.why: The switch joins all the wired devices, and its PoE ports can also power devices that have no outlet, such as the access point.

devs.name: Access point
devs.why: With PoE the access point needs just one Ethernet cable from the switch. That gives the office Wi-Fi without an outlet in the ceiling.

devs.name: File server
devs.why: A server is wired to a switch port so that it gets a steady, fast link and keeps one address.

devs.name: Hub
devs.why: A hub repeats every signal to all ports, with no MAC table and no PoE. It is old gear and a switch replaces it.

devs.name: Fiber media converter
devs.why: A converter changes fiber to copper. The hand-off here is already an Ethernet copper cable, so none is needed.

devs.name: Dial-up modem
devs.why: A dial-up modem uses a phone line and an RJ-11 connector and is far too slow. It has no role in this design.

q.title: Put the troubleshooting steps in order
q.scenario: A user in the front office says the shared printer stopped working this morning. You are the help desk technician. Build the response in a sensible order. Some ideas do not belong. Add the steps in the order they should happen.
q.ticket: TCK-5021: front-office printer not printing. Other users have not been asked yet.

rules.text: Ask what changed, when it began and who else is affected
rules.why: Gathering facts first tells you whether this is one user or the whole office, and what changed. Everything after it depends on this.

rules.text: Form a theory, such as the printer is offline or its cable is loose
rules.why: From the facts you pick the most likely cause. A theory gives your next test a target instead of random clicking.

rules.text: Test the theory by checking the printer screen and pinging its address
rules.why: A test shows if the theory is right. If it is not, you go back and form another one.

rules.text: Fix it, for example by reseating the cable or turning the printer back online
rules.why: You act once a tested theory points at a cause. A small, simple fix is tried first.

rules.text: Have the user print a page and check the other users can print
rules.why: Verifying proves the whole problem is solved for everyone, not just that you stopped working on it.

rules.text: Record the cause, the fix and the result in the ticket
rules.why: Notes let the next technician solve the same fault faster and show the work that was done.

rules.text: Replace the printer at once to be safe
rules.why: Replacing before any test costs money and may not fix a loose cable or an offline setting.

rules.text: Close the ticket before the user has tried printing
rules.why: Closing without confirmation can leave the user still blocked and the record wrong.

before.why: You need the facts before you can guess a cause.
There must be a theory before you can test it.
Test first, so you only fix what is really wrong.
Verify after the fix, since there is nothing to verify before it.

last.why: Documenting comes last because the ticket must show the cause, the fix and the confirmed result.

q.title: Find the probing in the firewall log
q.scenario: The unit's firewall protects a public web server at 203.0.113.10. The security monitor flagged a burst of denied connections. Mark every line that belongs to the suspicious activity, then say what the log shows.
q.ticket: Alert 3307: many DENY entries in a few seconds. Read the log only. No changes are asked.

lines.why: An inside PC browsing the web over HTTPS, which the policy permits. Nothing unusual.
An outside host tried an FTP port on the public server and was denied. It is the first probe of a series.
The same outside host, in the same second as the FTP probe, now tries SSH. A new port every try is the sign of a scan.
An inside device asking a public time server for the time. NTP on UDP 123 is expected and permitted.
Telnet is the third port in a row from the same address. It is another probe.
A different outside host reaching the public web server on 443, which the rule allows. This is an ordinary visitor.
Remote Desktop is a favorite target. The same source is still stepping through ports.
A PC pinging its own gateway, which is normal and allowed.
File sharing on 445 is another common probe. Five ports in about three seconds from one source ends the doubt.

ask.label: What does this log show?
opts: A denial-of-service flood against one web port
Users on the inside breaking the web policy
One outside host probing many ports on the server, and the default deny blocking them
Normal web traffic that the firewall blocked by mistake
ask.why: One source tries a different port each time, and the default-deny rule blocks every one of them. That is a port scan: a search for open doors, with the firewall doing its job.
